body:
Building new homes on green belt land is the only realistic way to ease the housing shortage around large cities.

To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Old buildings of historic value should be protected from demolition, even when this slows down the construction of new homes.

Do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Councils in popular holiday areas should be allowed to charge much higher council tax on second homes that stand empty for most of the year.

To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

More and more city councils are reducing speed limits on residential streets to 30 kilometres per hour.

Do you think this is a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some people think that road space taken by new cycle lanes should be returned to cars, since many people still depend on their cars. Others believe that protected cycle lanes are essential for making cities safer and healthier.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

While some argue that councils should build homes on urban parks and playing fields to meet housing needs, others believe that green spaces are too valuable to lose.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Co-living schemes, where residents rent a private bedroom but share the kitchen and living room, are spreading in large cities. Some see them as an affordable option, while others think they are no substitute for a proper home.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some people think that governments should spend heavily on high-speed rail lines that could replace short domestic flights. Others argue that airlines serve travellers better and that rail projects cost too much for the benefit they bring.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Many rural areas have lost most of their bus services over the past decade, leaving older residents and young people without reliable access to shops, hospitals and jobs.

Why has this happened?

What can be done to restore bus services in the countryside?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

In many towns, street layouts are designed around fast-moving traffic, so that pedestrians have to cross wide roads with short crossing times and few places to rest.

What problems does this cause for older people?

What measures could make streets safer and easier to use for older residents?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

New buildings in cities around the world increasingly look alike, with glass office towers, identical blocks of flats and the same shopping centres, so that it is hard to tell one place from another.

Why has architecture become so similar in different places?

What measures can local planners take to protect the character of their towns?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Many cities now charge drivers who enter the busiest central areas during working hours.

Do you think the advantages of this policy outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Developers are converting old office buildings in city centres into small one-bedroom flats for single people and couples.

To what extent do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Ride-hailing apps have replaced many traditional taxis in large cities, and many passengers now book their journeys through a smartphone.

Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Many parents drive their children to school even when the journey is short and there is a safe route on foot or by bicycle.

Why do so many parents choose to drive?

What can schools and local councils do to encourage more children to walk or cycle?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Cities that need more homes can either build out onto farmland at the edge of town or build up by adding storeys and filling gaps in existing neighbourhoods.

Why do planners often favour one of these approaches over the other?

Which approach better protects the quality of life for people who already live in the city?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Many new homes are being built with much smaller gardens than homes of previous generations, or with no outdoor space at all.

Why are developers building homes with less outdoor space?

Should planning rules require every new home to have access to a private or shared garden?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
